Oedipus.definition: Oedipūs odis, m, *oi)di/pous, a king of Thebes, who solved the riddle of the Sphinx, C., O.—Prov.: Davus sum, non Oedipus, i. e. no diviner, T.

Orgetorix.definition: Orgetorīx īgis, m a chief of the Helvetii, Cs.

obductus.definition: obductus adj. P. of obduco, overspread, clouded, gloomy: obductā nocte, O.: fronte, H., Iu.

obex.definition: (ōbex, ōbicis) m and f ob+IA-, a bolt, bar, barrier, wall (only abl sing. and nom, acc. and abl plur.): obices portarum, L.: fultos emuniit obice postes, V.: obice firmo Clauserat, O.: maria tumescant Obicibus ruptis,…

obgannio.definition: ob-ganniō —, —, īre, to snarl at: ei alqd ad aurem, T.

obiacens.definition: ob-iacēns ntis, P. P. praes. of ob-iaceo, lying before, lying near, in the way: sarcinarum cumulus, L.: saxa pedibus, L.

obiectatio.definition: obiectātiō ōnis, f obiecto, a reproach, Cs.

obiecto.definition: obiectō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. obicio, to set against, oppose: caput fretis, i. e. dive, V.—Fig., to abandon, expose, endanger: se hostium telis, L.: eum periculis, S.: caput periclis, V.: pro cunctis unam animam, V.—T…

obiectus1.definition: obiectus adj. P. of obicio, lying before, opposite: nec visi obiectis silvis, because of the woods in front, Cs.: insula Alexandriae, Cs.: flumina, V.: obiectus fortunae, exposed: ad omnes casūs periculorum.—Plur n. a…

obiectus2.definition: (obiectus, ūs) m ob+IA-, a putting against, opposing: miles tectus plutei obiectu, Cs.: insula portum Efficit obiectu laterum, opposition, V.: molium obiectūs scandere (i. e. moles obiectas), Ta.

obiratus.definition: ob-īrātus adj., angered, angry: fortunae, L.

obitus.definition: obitus (ūs), m ob+1 I-, an approach, visit, T.—A going down, setting: siderum: signorum, V.—Downfall, ruin, destruction, death: regis: post eorum obitum, Cs.: Difficiles obitūs, painful death, V.: post obitum vestrum,…

obiurgatio.definition: obiūrgātiō ōnis, f obiurgo, a chiding, reproof, rebuke, scolding, remonstrance: ut obiurgatio contumeliā careat: lenior.

obiurgator.definition: obiūrgātor ōris, m obiurgo, a chider, scold noster.— Plur: benevoli.

obiurgatorius.definition: obiūrgātōrius adj. obiurgator, chiding, scolding: epistula.

obiurgo.definition: ob-iūrgō āvī, ātus, āre, to chide, scold, blame, rebuke, reprove: ad obiurgandum causa, T.: Caelium: me de Pompei familiaritate, moderately: cum obiurgarer, quod nimio gaudio paene desiperem.—To urge, adjure, exhort e…

oblique.definition: oblīquē adv. obliquus, athwart, obliquely: ferri.—Indirectly, covertly: alqm castigare, Ta.

oblitus2.definition: oblītus adj. P. of obliviscor, forgetful, unmindful, not remembering: sui: veterum honorum, O.—Forgetful, regardless, indifferent, neglectful: Illum gementem Obliti relinquunt, V.: pectus, Ct.: mei, i. e. of my dignit…

oblivium.definition: oblīvium ī, n obliviscor, forgetfulness, oblivion: sententiam oblivio transmittere, T.—Usu. plur: longa oblivia potant, V.: Ducere oblivia vitae, H.: Herculeae oblivia laudis Acta tibi, that you have forgotten, O.

obnixe.definition: obnīxē adv., with all one's strength, strenuously, obstinately: omnia Facturus, T.

obnixus.definition: obnīxus (not obnīsus), adj. P. of obnitor, strenuous, firm, resolute: (velim) obnixos vos impetum hostium excipere, L.: curam sub corde premebat, V.: non cedere, V.

obnoxie.definition: obnoxiē adv. obnoxius, slavishly, timidly: sententias dicere, L.

obnubilus.definition: ob-nūbilus adj., clouded over: tenebris loca, Enn. ap. C.

oboediens.definition: oboediēns (not obēd-), entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of oboedio, obedient, subject, compliant: Omnia oboedientia sunt, reduced to subjection, S.: cuius vis omnis in consensu oboedientium esset, the obedient, L.: …

obscene.definition: obscēnē (obscaenē) adv. with comp. obscenus, immodestly, indecently, obscenely: dici: obscenius excitata.

obscure.definition: obscūrē adv. with comp. and sup. obscurus, darkly, obscurely: cernere, dimly.—Fig., covertly, closely, secretly: agere: alqd ferre: obscurius iniqui, more secretly: quam obscurissime.

obsequens.definition: obsequēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of obsequor, yielding, compliant, obsequious, accommodating: patri, T.: legiones nobis: Persae obsequentiores, Cu.

obsero1.definition: obserō āvī, ātus, āre 1 SER-, to bolt, bar, fasten, shut up: ostium intus, T.: aedificia, L.: aurīs, H.

obsero2.definition: ob-serō sēvī, situs, ere, to sow, plant: terram frugibus.— P. perf., covered over, covered, strewn, filled: obsiti virgultis colles, L.: pomis Rura, O.: aeger pannis annisque, T.: montes nivibus, Cu.: Io iam setis obs…

observans.definition: observāns antis, adj. with sup. P. of observo, watchful, attentive, respectful: homo tui: observantissimus mei.

obses.definition: obses idis (gen plur. obsidum, rarely obsidium, Cs., L.), m and f SED-, a hostage: obsides uti inter sese dent, exchange, Cs.: Cretensibus obsides imperavit: multi Romanis dediti obsides, S.: alqm obsidem retinere, as…

obsideo.definition: obsideō ēdī, essus, ēre ob+sedeo, to sit, stay, remain, abide: domi, T.—To beset, haunt, frequent: umbilicum terrarum.—In war, to hem in, beset, besiege, invest, blockade: quod (oppidum) neque capi neque obsideri pote…

obsidium1.definition: obsidium ī, n ob+SED-, a siege, blockade: obsidio circumdare, Ta.

obsidium2.definition: obsidium ī, n obses, the condition of a hostage, hostageship: obsidio nobis datus, Ta.

obsolefio.definition: obsolefiō —, fierī 1 OL-, to wear out, be spoiled: obsolefiebant dignitatis insignia, became worthless.

obsolete.definition: (obsolētē) adv. obsoletus, in an old style, poorly, shabbily.— Only comp: obsoletius vestitus.

obsoletus.definition: obsolētus adj. with comp. P. of obsolesco, old, worn out, thrown off: erat veste obsoletā, L.: esse vestitu obsoletiore: homo, shabby: tectum, ruinous, H.: verba, obsolete.—Common, ordinary, poor, mean, low: crimina: …

obstans.definition: (obstāns, ntis) n P. of obsto, an obstruction. —Only plur: pellere obstantia, i. e. open the body, H.: obstantia silvarum amoliri, Ta.

obstinate.definition: obstinātē adv. obstinatus, firmly, inflexibly, resolutely, obstinately: operam dat, T.: negari, Cs.: haec credita, L.

obstitus.definition: obstitus adj. P. of obsisto, opposite, opposing; hence, in augury, struck by lightning.—Plur. n. as subst: obstita pianto.

obtentus1.definition: obtentus P. of obtendo, and of obtineo.

obtentus2.definition: (ob-tentus, ūs) m obtendo, a drawing over, spreading over.— Only dat. and abl sing.: obtentu frondis, V.—Fig., a cover, pretext: cognominis, L.: rei p., Ta.

obtexo.definition: ob-texō —, —, ere, to weave over, overspread, cover: caelum obtexitur umbrā, V.

obticeo.definition: obticeō —, —, ēre ob+taceo, to be silent: Virgo obticet, T.

obtunsus.definition: obtūnsus adj. P. of obtundo, see obtūsus.

obtusus.definition: obtūsus or obtūnsus adj. with comp. P. of obtundo, blunt, dull, obtuse: vomer, V.—Fig., blunt, dull, weak, faint: cui (animo) obtusior sit acies: obtunsa pectora, insensible, V.: ne obtunsior usus Sit genitali arvo, t…

obvallatus.definition: ob-vāllātus P., fortified, intrenched, made irrefutable: locus omni ratione.

obversor.definition: ob-versor ātus, ārī, dep., to make an appearance, show oneself: partem eorum Carthagini obversari dici, L.—Fig., to hover before, appear: nihi ante oculos obversatur rei p. dignitas: in somnis, L.

obversus.definition: obversus adj. P. of obverto, turned against, directed towards: faciem obversus in agmen, O. —Turned towards, engaged in: militum studiis, Ta.—Plur m. as subst, opponents, Ta.

obviam.definition: ob-viam or ob viam adv., in the way, towards, against, to meet, in face of: obviam conabar tibi, was hurrying to meet you, T.: si obviam contra veniretur, an advance should be made, Cs.: fit obviam Clodio, meets: obvi…

occasus2.definition: occāsus ūs, m ob+1 CAD-, a falling, going down, setting: Maiae, V.: cum occasu solis, at sunset, S.—The sunset, west: ab ortu ad occasum: ager Longus in occasum, V.: Prospicit occasūs, O.—Fig., downfall, ruin, destruc…

occidens.definition: occidēns entis, m P. of 2 occido, the sunset, west, occident: ab occidente, S.: ab oriente ad occidentem.

occido1.definition: occīdō cīdī, cīsus, ere ob+caedo, to strike down, knock down: me pugnis, T.—To cut down, cut off, kill, slay: si aliam (noxiam) admisero, occidito, T.: fortissime pugnans occiditur, Cs.: exercitūs occidione occisi, an…

occido2.definition: occidō cidī, cāsus, ere ob+cado, to fall down, fall: ut alii super alios occiderent, L.— To go down, set: iam occidente sole, Pac. ap. C.: donec lux occidat, Iu.—To fall, perish, die, be slain: quā (securi) multi occi…

occulte.definition: occultē adv. with comp. and sup. occultus, in concealment, in secret, secretly, privately: neque id occulte fert, makes no secret of it, T.: ea nunc occulte cuniculis oppugnatur: loqui cetera, S.: proficisci, Cs.: lab…

occultus.definition: occultus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of occulo, covered up, hidden, concealed, secret: locus, S.: occultiores insidiae: quo occultior esset eius adventus, Cs.: si quid erit occultius: cum res occultissimas aperueris: …

occupatus.definition: occupātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of occupo, taken up, engrossed, absorbed, occupied, employed, busy, engaged: In alio amore, T.: in opere, Cs.: opere, L.: non occupatorum amicorum adsiduitas: in eo, ut, etc., N.:…

ocius.definition: ōcius adv. comp., with sup. ōcissimē neut. of ocior, more quickly, more speedily, sooner: idque ocius faciet, si, etc.: recreantur ocius: serius ocius Sors exitura, sooner or later, H.: Angulus iste feret tus ocius uv…

octavum.definition: octāvum adv. octavus, for the eighth time: tribuni refecti, L.

octiens.definition: octiēns (-ēs) adv. num. octo, eight times.

octingentesimus.definition: octingentēsimus adj. num. octingenti, the eight hundredth: annus.

octipes.definition: octipēs edis, adj. octo+pes, eight-footed. Cancer, O.

octogensimus.definition: octōgēnsimus (-gēsimus) adj. num. octoginta, the eightieth: annus: solstitia, Iu.

octogiens.definition: octōgiēns (-iēs) num adv. octoginta, eighty times: sestertium (centena milia).

octoiugis.definition: octōiugis e, adj. octo+IV-, eight in a team: octoiuges ire, i. e. eight in a body, L.

octophoros.definition: octōphoros (octāph-) adj., carried by eight bearers: lectica.— As subst n., a litter with eight bearers: hominem portare octophoro.

odiose.definition: odiōsē adv. odiosus, hatefully, vexatiously: cessat, T.: dicere: interpellare.

odoratus1.definition: odōrātus adj. P. of odoro, that has a smell, odorous, scented, sweet-smelling, fragrant: lignum, V.: odoratis ignibus, O.: rosā capillos, H.: dux, i. e. of the Assyrians, Pr.

odoratus2.definition: odōrātus ūs, m odoror, a smelling, smell: eorum iucundus.— The sense of smell.

odoror.definition: odōror ātus, ārī, dep. odor, to smell at, smell out, scent: cibum, H.—Fig., to aspire to, aim at: hunc decemviratum, to be snuffing after.—To search out, trace out, investigate: pecuniam: tu velim ex Fabio odorere: od…

odos1.definition: odōs ōris, m 2 OD-, a smell, scent, odor: omnis odor ad supera fertur: odorem avide trahere naribus, Ph.: florum.—A pleasant odor, perfume, perfumery, essences, spices: odore capi: ara fumat odore, incense, H.: croceo…

oesus.definition: oesus (ūs), m (old form of usus), C.

offensa.definition: offēnsa ae, f P. of offendo, disfavor, displeasure, offence, hatred, enmity: magnā in offensā esse apud Pompeium: Offensā mei, out of hatred for me, O.—A violation of law, offence, crime: vetus atque tacenda, Iu.—An i…

offero.definition: offerō (obf-) obtulī (opt-), oblātus, offerre ob +fero, to bring before, present, offer, show, exhibit: illis fors obtulerat adventum meum, T.: me perditum illi adflictumque: se consulibus ferociter, L.: quā novā re o…

officiose.definition: officiōsē adv. with comp. officiosus, courteously, obligingly: factum: (fecit) illa officiosius.

offirmatus.definition: (offīrmātus) adj. P. of offirmo, firm, obstinate.—Only comp: voluntas offirmatior.

oleaginus.definition: oleāginus adj. olea, of the olive-tree: radix, V.: virgulae, N.

oleaster.definition: oleaster strī, m olea, the wild olive-tree, oleaster: collis vestitus oleastro, S., C., V., O.

olens.definition: olēns entis, adj. P. of oleo, smelling, odorous: flos bene olentis anethi, V.—Sweet-smelling, fragrant, odoriferous: rami, V.: mentae, O.—Of an ill odor, rank, musty: maritus (i. e. hircus), H.: Membra, V.: fornix, H.…

olivom.definition: olīvom or olīvum ī, n oliva, oil: pingue, V.: perfundere piscī s olivo, H., O.—An ointment, unguent, Ct., Pr.—Fig., the palaestra (because wrestlers were anointed): cur olivum vitat? H.

olla.definition: ōlla ae, f VC-, a pot, jar, C., H., Iu.—Prov.: ipsa holera olla legit, the pot culls its own herbs, Ct.

omissus.definition: 'omissus adj. with comp. P. of omitto, negligent, heedless: animo esse omisso, T.: ab re Omissiores, in respect of property, T.'

omniparens.definition: omniparēns tis, adj. omnis+parens, allbearing, all-producing: terra, V.

onager.definition: onager ī, m, o)/nagros, a wild ass, V.

onerarius.definition: onerārius adj. onus, of burden, of transport, for freight: navis: iumenta, L.—As subst f. (sc. navis), a merchant-vessel, transport.

onyx.definition: 'onyx ychis, m, o)/nuc, a vessel of onyx, onyxbox: nardi parvus, H.: murrheus, for ointment, Pr.'

operor.definition: operor ātus, ārī, dep. opus, to work, labor, toil, take pains, be busied, devote oneself: in cute curandā, H.: rei p., L.: Conubiis arvisque novis, V.: studio operatus inhaesi, engrossed, O.—Of religious observances, …

operose.definition: operōsē adv. operosus, painfully, laboriously, carefully: fieri: vina condita, O.

opinatus.definition: opīnātus adj. P. of opinor, supposed, imagined, fancied: bona, mala.

opiniosus.definition: (opīniōsus) adj. opinio, full of hypotheses. —Only sup: opiniosissimi homines (dub.).

opinus.definition: (opīnus) adj. 2 AP-, supposing, believing; only in in-opinus, nec-opinus.

opipare.definition: opiparē adv. opiparus, richly, sumptuously: edere: apparatum convivium.

opitulor.definition: opitulor ātus, ārī, dep. ops+TAL-, to bring aid, help, aid, assist, succor: mihi: inopiae, relieve, S.: permultum ad dicendum.

oppido.definition: oppidō adv. abl. of oppidum, very, very much, completely, exceedingly, exactly, precisely: iratus, T.: ridiculus: inter se differunt: adulescens, L.: oppido quam breve intervallum, exceedingly short, L.

opportune.definition: opportūnē adv. with sup. opportunus, filly, seasonably, opportunely: ehem opportune, well met, T.: venisse: locus captus ad eam rem: opportune inritandis animis litterae adlatae, L.: nuntiis opportunissime adlatis, Cs.

oppositus1.definition: oppositus adj. P. of oppono, standing against, opposed, opposite: Mons Cebenna, Cs.: luna soli: contra Zancleïa saxa Rhegion, O.— Fig.: propugnaculum istis ipsis nationibus.

oppositus2.definition: (oppositus ūs),m oppono, a placing against, opposing, opposition (only abl sing. and acc plur.): laterum nostrorum oppositūs pollicemur: solem lunae oppositu deficere.

optandus.definition: 'optandus adj. P. of opto, desirable: otium, divitiae, optanda alias, S.: maxime fuit optandum Caecinae, ut, etc.'

optato.definition: optātō adv. neut. abl. of optatus, as desired, in fulfilment of wishes: advenis, you are welcome, T.: mihi veneris: ventis aestate coortis, V.

optatus.definition: optātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of opto, wished, desired, longed for, welcome, desirable, pleasing: occasio, T.: rumores: Iovis epulae, H.: quid est quod exteris nationibus optatius esse possit?: optatissimum bene…

optime1.definition: optimē bonus; for * bone.—Of manner, well, better, best: ager bene cultus: olere, agreeably, V.: succedere, prosperously, T.: optione vendere, dear: emere honorem, cheaply, V.: habitare, in good style, N.: optime vide…

optio1.definition: optiō ōnis, f 2 AP-, choice, free choice, liberty to choose, privilege, option: optionem Carthaginiensium faciunt, ut vel, etc., S.: utro frui malis, optio sit tua: hiberna legionis eligendi.

optio2.definition: optiō ōnis, m 1 optio, an adjutant, Ta.

opulenter.definition: 'opulenter adv. with comp. opulens, richly, sumptuously, splendidly: colore me, S.: ludos opulentius facere, L.'

ora1.definition: ōra ae, f 1 AS-, an extremity, border, brim, edge, rim, margin, end, boundary, limit: omnes spectant ad carceris oras, at the barriers, Enn. ap. C.: (clipei), V.: summa (vestis), O.: regiones, quarum nulla esset ora: …

ora2.definition: ōra ae, f a cable, ship's line, head-line: resolutis oris, L.: trahunt scalas orasque, L.

oratum.definition: ōrātum ī, n P. n. of oro, an entreaty, supplication: quom orata eius reminiscor, T.

oratus.definition: (ōrātus, ūs) m oro, a praying, request, entreaty; only abl sing.: oratu tuo.

ordinatus.definition: ōrdinātus adj. P. of ordino, arranged, ordained: cursū s, appointed.

orgia.definition: orgia ōrum, n, o)/rgia, the orgies, nocturnal festival of Bacchus: nocturni Bacchi, V.—Secret frantic revels, orgies, Iu.: Itala, the mysteries of love in the Latin tongue, Pr.

oriens.definition: oriēns entis, m P. of orior, the rising sun, morning sun: saevus, V.— The East, Orient: ab oriente ad occidentem: spoliis Orientis onustus, V.: Orientis ora, H.—A day: Septimus hinc, O.

oriundus.definition: oriundus adj. P. of orior, descended, sprung, originating, born: o sanguen dis oriundum, Enn. ap. C.: ex Etruscis, L.: oriundi ab Syracusis, exsule avo, L.: Albā oriundum sacerdotium, L.

ornate.definition: ōrnātē adv. with comp. and sup. orno, ornamentally, ornately, elegantly: convivium apparare: pars causae perorata: dici ornatius: egit ornatissime causam.

ornatus1.definition: ōrnātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of orno, fitted out, furnished, provided, supplied, equipped, accoutred: sapiens plurimis artibus: equus, L.: elephantus, N.: naves omni genere armorum ornatissimae, Cs.: Graecia co…

ornatus2.definition: ōrnātus ūs, m orno, splendid dress, fine attire, apparel: venio ornatu prologi, dressed as, T.: regalis: arma ornatumque mutaverant, S.: omnem ornatum flammā cremari, head-dress, V.: corporis ornatum exuere, Iu.— Fig.…

orsa.definition: ōrsa ōrum, n P. plur. n. of ordior, an undertaking, attempt: tanti operis, L.—Words, speech: sic orsa vicissim Ore refert, V.

orsus1.definition: ōrsus P. of ordior; see also orsa.

orsus2.definition: (ōrsus, ūs) m ordior, a beginning, undertaking, attempt (only acc plur.): vanos pectoris orsūs.

ortus1.definition: ortus adj. P. of orior, sprung, descended, born: ab illo: a liberatoribus patriae, L.: ex eodem oco, T.: ex concubinā, S.: ex patricio sanguine, <*>.: Orte Saturno, H.: sorore eius, L.: regiā stirpe, Cu.

ortus2.definition: ortus ūs, m orior, a rising: ante ortum solis, sunrise, Cs.: ab ortu ad occasum, from east to west. solis, the east: primi sub lumina solis et ortū s, V.: rutilo ab ortu, O.: ad umbram lucis ab ortu, from morning till…

oryx.definition: oryx (ygis), m, o)/ruc, a gazelle, wild goat, Iu.

os1.definition: ōs ōris (no gen plur.), n the mouth: ad haec omnia percipienda os est aptissimum: tenerum pueri, H.: os loquentis Opprimere, O.: e foliis natos Ore legunt (apes), V.: Gallica Temperat ora frenis, i. e. controls the ho…

os2.definition: os ossis, gen plur. ossium, n a bone.—Sing: devoratum, Ph.: ferrum ex osse revolsum est, O.: duro sudem vix osse revulsit, O.—Plur: cur hunc dolorem cineri eius atque ossibus inussisti?: ossa legere (after burning a c…

oscitans.definition: ōscitāns ntis, adj. P. of oscito, listless, sluggish, lazy, negligent: interea oscitantes opprimi, T.: quae Epicurus oscitans halucinatus est, half asleep: alites, Ct.

osculor.definition: ōsculor ātus, ārī, dep. osculum, to kiss: mitto osculari, T.: filium.—To embrace, value, prize: inimicum meum.

ostentum.definition: ostentum ī, n P. n. of ostendo, a prodigy, wonder, portent: cum magnorum periculorum metus ex ostentis portenderetur: Victus ostentis, quae plurima viderat, O.

ostentus2.definition: (ostentus, ūs) m ostendo, a showing, display, sign, proof: ut Iugurthae scelerum ostentui essem, S.—A pretence: illa deditionis signa ostentui credere, S.

otiose.definition: ōtiōsē adv. otiosus, at leisure, at ease, without occupation: vivere: inambulare in foro, L.— Calmly, quietly, without haste, gently, gradually: contemplari unumquodque: omnia agere, L.— Free from fear, quietly, fearl…

ovans.definition: ovāns antis, adj. P. of ovo, exulting, joyful, triumphant: socii comitentur ovantes, V.: ovantes gutture corvi, i. e. uttering exultant cries, V.: patria, Iu.: currūs, triumphal chariot, Pr.
